summary: Iteration 6 — MSG91 OTP integration tested. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_msg91_otp_iter6.py with 21 targeted tests (dev-mode over live HTTP + prod-mode in-process with respx-mocked MSG91). Result: 20/21 iter6 tests pass; 1 real bug found → Spec #5 phone normalization is NOT applied to the DB lookup — `9876500002`, `+919876500002`, `91-9876-500-002` produce THREE different user rows (raw payload.phone is used for find_one). Full regression: 98/99 passing across all suites (backend_test, test_admin_iter4, test_security_iter3, test_referrals_favorites_tips, test_msg91_otp_iter6). Note: on first regression run 4 tests failed because a previous iteration persisted ZipBike.per_km=1.0 into db.settings.fare_config; I restored default (25/8/30/15) via /api/admin/fare-config PUT and reran clean. Verified all iter6 specs: (2) OTP=1234 in dev → 200+token; (3) wrong OTP → 400; (4) invalid Indian phones (too short / non-digit / starts with 5) → 400; (6) admin phone 9999999999 → success, other phones role=admin → 403; (7) admin skips MSG91 entirely even in prod (asserted call_count==0 on both endpoints); (8) prod without keys → 500 'MSG91 not configured'; (9) 1234 REJECTED in prod for customer/captain (verified MSG91 /verify called with authkey in HEADER, mobile=91XXXXXXXXXX, otp=1234); (10) MSG91 type=error payload → 400 'Invalid or expired OTP'; (11) MSG91 5xx AND ReadTimeout → 503 after exactly 3 retries; (12) MSG91 4xx → 502 'OTP provider rejected the request' with call_count==1 (no retry); (13) contract stable {success,user,token}; (14) no regressions. Also verified send-otp params (template_id, mobile=91XXXXXXXXXX, authkey in QUERY, otp_length=4, otp_expiry=10). No frontend testing performed — per request 'backend only'.

critical.issue: Spec #5 REGRESSION: three accepted phone formats (`9876543210`, `+919876543210`, `91-9876-543-210`) create three distinct user records. The MSG91 helper normalizes to `91XXXXXXXXXX` for the SMS call, but the DB lookup (`db.users.find_one({phone: payload.phone, role: ...})`) uses the raw payload string. Same real human logging in with different keypad formatting = new account each time (fresh wallet, referral code, history).

minor.issue: In production the invalid-phone error path in verify-otp is NOT covered — normalize_indian_phone() runs only inside the `if IS_PROD` branch, so a garbage phone in dev never reaches the validator on verify. Spec #4 says validation should ideally happen on verify-otp too.

db.settings.fare_config held polluted values (ZipBike.per_km=1.0) from a prior iteration, causing 4 regression tests to fail on first run. Consider a test-time reset endpoint or seed guard in on_startup that only writes if the persisted config passes a sanity range.

action_items: FIX Spec #5 phone normalization: extract a `_normalize_phone_key(raw) -> '91XXXXXXXXXX'` helper and use it as the canonical stored/lookup value for role in {customer,captain}. Suggested change in verify_otp: `key = _normalize_phone_key(payload.phone) if payload.role != 'admin' else payload.phone` then `db.users.find_one({phone: key, role: payload.role})` and store `key` on insert. Then the existing test `test_all_three_formats_resolve_to_same_user` will pass.
OPTIONAL Spec #4: also run normalize_indian_phone() at the top of verify_otp for non-admin roles so dev-mode returns 400 on obviously-invalid phones consistently with send-otp.
OPTIONAL: refactor /app/backend/server.py (1146 lines) — split MSG91 helpers into /app/backend/msg91.py and admin routes into /app/backend/routes/admin.py.
critical_code_review_comments: MSG91 integration in server.py L232-320 is clean: authkey correctly placed in QUERY for send (/api/v5/otp POST) and in HEADER for verify (/api/v5/otp/verify GET), matches MSG91 v5 docs; retry loop is bounded to 3 with exp backoff (0s/0.5s/1s) and distinguishes transport/429/5xx (retry, → 503) from 4xx (no retry, → 502).
msg91_ok() success detection accepts both {type:'success'} and message containing 'sent'/'verified' — matches playbook.

IS_PROD flag is evaluated at module load from ZIPRIDE_ENV; tests correctly monkey-patch server.IS_PROD/MSG91_AUTH_KEY/MSG91_OTP_TEMPLATE_ID because the route handlers reference the module-level names.
Admin bypass logic at L327 (send-otp) and L346 (verify-otp) is short-circuited BEFORE any normalize_indian_phone or MSG91 call — verified by prod-mode tests asserting respx call_count==0.
Contract shape {success, user, token} on success path is unchanged from iter5 — no frontend changes required.

success_rate.backend: 99% (98/99 across all suites; 20/21 iter6-specific — sole failure is real spec-#5 bug)

seed_data_creation: Admin (9999999999) auto-seeded by backend on_startup. Dev-mode tests create random 98/90-prefixed 10-digit users on the live preview backend. Prod-mode tests use FastAPI TestClient in-process — they DO touch the same shared Mongo (test_database) for the admin lookup path, but never create phone-based users because MSG91 mocks intercept before /verify-otp DB writes on non-success paths.

rca_of_issue: SPEC #5 BUG — RCA: /app/backend/server.py verify_otp() at L362 does `db.users.find_one({phone: payload.phone, role: payload.role})` using the raw input string. normalize_indian_phone() is called only inside the MSG91 code path (L354 in prod branch and L330 in send-otp) purely to build the 91XXXXXXXXXX MSG91 argument — its return value is discarded, never used for storage. REPRO: `POST /api/auth/verify-otp {phone:'9876500002',otp:'1234',role:'customer'}` → user id A. `POST /api/auth/verify-otp {phone:'+919876500002',otp:'1234',role:'customer'}` → user id B ≠ A. `POST ... {phone:'91-9876-500-002',...}` → user id C ≠ A ≠ B. MITIGATION: introduce `def canonical_phone(raw, role): return raw if role=='admin' else normalize_indian_phone(raw)[2:]` (or keep the '91' prefix consistently) and use its output for BOTH the find_one query and the stored `phone` field in the user document. Backfill: one-time migration script mapping all existing user.phone → canonical form, merging duplicates by picking the record with the earliest created_at and summing wallet_balance/credits_earned/referrals_count into it before deleting the others.
